name: cifer
desc: Work on automating classical cipher cracking in C
why: Aims at automating classical cipher cracking in C, a fun cryptanalysis rabbit hole but an old, abandoned-looking project.

brief.what_it_is: Cifer is a project, described in its package metadata as work on automating classical cipher cracking in C. It ships two executables, cifer and cifer-dict. I could not read the project's own README or documentation, so this description comes from the Homebrew formula and the scout notes, not from the author. I cannot confirm what inputs the tools take or what they output.
brief.why_it_exists: The only stated purpose is automating the cracking of classical ciphers. The author's own framing was not available to me.
brief.install_notes: Nothing beyond the Homebrew formula is known. The formula lists the executables cifer and cifer-dict. No build, runtime, or configuration steps were visible to me.
brief.standout: The name cifer and the separate cifer-dict executable suggest a dictionary-driven cracking tool alongside a general one, but I could not verify this from any source. Nothing unusual is confirmed.
brief.status: Appears abandoned, but unverified. The homepage is a Google Code Archive page, and Google Code was shut down in 2016, so the project host itself is dead. The archive page loads only a JavaScript shell with no release or commit dates. The scout notes also call it old and abandoned-looking. I found no last release date, last commit, or README note.
brief.caveats: The homepage and the archive URL both returned only the Google Code Archive JavaScript shell, with no README text. The entry should not describe features, usage, or results beyond the formula description. Source code may exist in the archive, but I could not reach it. Licensing is unknown.
